purpose: Defines the operating principles for creating and revising ADRs: what to record, how to screen content, mutability, rejection handling, placement and numbering, tolerance zones, and a severity catalog.
summary: ADR definition: responsibility, what not to write, exception for approved designs, permanence and revision
Beneficiary is the AI about to propose alternatives, so rejection reasons must be thorough
Criteria for what to write: future plausible proposal and not answerable from code, rules or specs
Conditions for the optional scope box
Screening criteria table: reject, revise and record, or insufficient
ADR is mutable: rewrite sections, never renumber, no change-log section
Rejected decisions are folded into the same section, with old option moved to alternatives
Placement per feature, single file per feature, numbering via next-spec-id skill
Gray zone tolerance table of allowed and disallowed practices
tasks: Deciding whether content deserves an ADR
Reviewing an ADR or judging review findings
Handling a revoked or corrected decision
Assigning an ADR number and placing the file
Proposing an alternative design and checking whether it was already considered
title: ADR（アーキテクチャ決定記録）運用原則
